chunks: 2754 - Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:
I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who enters Makkah once, twice, or three times in a year. What should he do?
He said: “When he enters, then let him enter reciting the talbiyah, and when he leaves, then let him leave having exited iḥrām.”

key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the sacred city being entered repeatedly
key_terms.مُحِلًّا: being out of iḥrām or having exited the state of iḥrām
key_terms.يَخْرُجْ: leaves, referring to departure from Makkah
key_terms.يَدْخُلُ: enters, referring to entry into Makkah
key_terms.ٱلسَّنَةِ: the year, specifying the time frame of repeated entry

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he enters Makkah multiple times in one year?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who enters Makkah multiple times within a year. Imam Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام instructs that he should enter in a state associated with talbiyah and leave in a state of having become lawful again, indicating the regulation of repeated entry and exit in relation to iḥrām.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2754 - Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (as) about a man who enters Mecca once, twice, or three times in a year. What should he do?
Imam (as) said: "When he enters, he should do so in the state of ihram, reciting the Talbiyah, and when he leaves, he should exit in the state of non-ihram."
